messages:
jess (support): Incoming ticket — customer reporting embeddings API returning 768-d vectors but their code expects 1536. Also seeing intermittent timeouts and a few 502s. They upgraded our TS SDK yesterday.
sahil (eng): can you paste the raw request/response (headers + body) and the SDK version? any client-side batching config?
jess (support): SDK: @redwood/ts-sdk v2.4.1. Request payload: 
```
POST /v1/embeddings
{ model: 'open-sim-embed', input: ['a', 'b', 'c'], batch_size: 128 }
```
Response (truncated): 
```
200 OK
{ data: [ { embedding: [ /* 768 floats */ ] }, ... ] }
```
Client logs show: `timeout after 8s` on many requests, and server logs show some 502s from runtime when batching spikes.
mike (platform): any recent model routing changes? Was there a deployment that introduced a 768-d model variant that might be auto-falling back?
eva (eng-ml): yes — we onboarded a quantized small variant (open-sim-embed-small) with 768 dims for cost tiering. Smart routing can fallback when capacity constrained. That would explain returned dims if the request hit that variant. But SDK should surface model name in response metadata; did the customer see model field?
jess (support): customer says response metadata is empty. TS SDK v2.4.1 apparently strips some headers for embeddings responses in recent patch. Repro steps from customer: set batch_size 128, concurrency 32, run stream of 10k inputs. After ~300 requests some requests return 768 vectors and some requests timeout.
sahil (eng): two problems: 1) dim mismatch due to routing to small variant; 2) timeouts related to large batching + concurrency causing queueing in runtime and occasional 502. For (1) we should make SDK validate returned dimension vs expected model profile and raise a clear error instead of silently returning wrong length. For (2) need to advise on batching defaults and increase request-side timeout + apply backoff.
mike (platform): agree. Immediate mitigation for customer: pin model to `open-sim-embed@v1.2` (non-small variant) in the request so routing won't fallback. Also reduce client batch_size to 64 and concurrency to 8. Increase client timeout to 20s. That avoids the overloaded queue path.
jess (support): passing those to customer now. They asked for a repro script so platform/eng can reproduce. I attached a small ts snippet they used: 
```
const client = new RedwoodEmbeddings({ apiKey: process.env.RW_KEY, model: 'open-sim-embed' })
await client.embedBatch(inputs, { batchSize: 128, concurrency: 32, timeoutMs: 8000 })
```
They said switching to `model: 'open-sim-embed@v1.2'` fixed dims immediately.
eva (eng-ml): root cause: smart-routing allowed fallback to quantized small variant under load. SDK patch removed model metadata in v2.4.1 by accident (we previously returned `x-model` header but serdes got changed). So customer couldn't detect mismatch. Also the runtime batching queue metric spiked because client batch_size 128 + concurrency 32 produced requests that exceeded our continuous-batching budget, leading to eviction/502s.
sahil (eng): action items: 
- short: recommend pin and lower batch/concurrency for affected customers.
- mid: release a hotfix for TS SDK that restores model metadata on embeddings responses and adds a quick-dimension-check (throw an explicit error if dims != expected for model).
- mid: add client-side example config defaults (batch_size 64, concurrency 8, timeout 15s) in docs.
- long: runtime should annotate responses with model variant and expose reason for fallback if routing downgraded capacity. Also consider rate-limiting heuristics for large batches.
mike (platform): I'll open infra ticket to add a runtime trace field `serving_variant` in response metadata and a dashboard to surface when small-variant routing is used. Also will add a runtime safe-guard: if batch + concurrency > platform threshold, reject with 429 early instead of queueing to 502.
ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2026 — embeddings-dim-fallback. Linked to ticket #9842. Severity: P2.

jess (support): quick workaround communicated and customer confirmed dims fixed after pinning. They're going to wait for SDK hotfix. They also asked if we can auto-detect and warn in the SDK rather than failing app logic. Can we add a non-breaking warning first?
sahil (eng): hotfix flow: (1) restore metadata header + deprecation note, (2) add opt-in strictMode=true in SDK which will throw on mismatch; default=warn in minor release, strict in next major. We'll also include retry/backoff helpers: exponential backoff with jitter, default maxRetries=4, per-request timeout default 15s.
eva (eng-ml): for regression tests add unit test that simulates mixed-dim responses and assert SDK behavior when strictMode toggled. Also add e2e with runtime under simulated load to catch the queueing pattern.
mike (platform): timeline: infra ticket assigned, will prioritize dashboard + 429 guard (ETA 3 days). SDK hotfix (v2.4.2) to restore headers and add dim-check/warn (ETA 48 hours). Docs update same day.
jess (support): closing loop with customer: patch scheduled, provided pinned model workaround + config recommendations. Customer thanked us and will verify after SDK patch. Marking thread resolved for now. :thumbsup:
sahil (eng): follow-ups: please capture postmortem notes in #postmortems once infra changes land. Also capture churn metric: number of customers affected, to evaluate if routing default should change.
jess (support): will track. Adding this to weekly support sync notes.
